answer: A farm running 78 keys as a result forfeits that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation inexpensive. Because the tundra stake is held until the gale settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the sable audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 42% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a low-cost one. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
